Maintaining this document: maintenance guide.

Five ordered routes through the portfolio. The Tool Atlas answers 'what is this tool and where is it used?' one tool at a time; these paths teach one idea at a time across several projects, so a reader does not have to guess which repository to open first.

Status. First edition, 6 October 2026. 25 of the 26 stages were run. 21 passed as written (stage 1.3 with a setup deviation, and five stages on a scratch Node 24 install; stages 1.5 and 5.5 with commands taken from the project's own documentation, because the outline named none). Stage 2.4 passed after a dotnet restore that its command assumes (finding 10). Stage 2.5 passed with two deviations (port 8001, and the gate run in a Linux container on normalised reports; finding 8). Stage 4.3 ran and reported real image-pin drift, as it is designed to; the pin has since been refreshed (finding 11). Stage 4.4 failed to start on Windows on 6 October and passed on 7 October after the probe was fixed (finding 7). 1 stage was not run (4.2), because its Docker stack was in use by another session. It is labelled in place. Stages 5.3 and 5.4 failed in the cloud container on a browser-build mismatch and passed as written on a machine with the matching browsers.

1. How to use this

Read the paths in order 1 to 4; path 5 can be read alone. Every stage has the same parts.

Part What it holds
Tool and where The Atlas entry, and the project and folder to open.
Read The decision record that explains the choice.
Do One command (or two), copied from the project's package.json or README.
Captured result What the command printed when run, with the duration. Not run: says so.
Watch for The common mistake. Drawn from a decision record or from the captured run.

Reading a Captured result is not the same as running the command. Counts will change as projects move; the durations are from one machine (section 2) and show scale, not a benchmark.

Projects still in progress. Two projects in these paths are not finished, and the stages that use them say so. saleor-graphql-automation (stages 3.4 and 4.2) is active: Phases 0 and 1 are done and Phase 2 is underway. tradeblotter-wpf-screenplay (stages 1.5 and 5.5) has TB-01 to TB-08A complete; TB-08B is blocked on a Ranorex licence and the project is parked.

2. How the stages were run

Each project was cloned from its local checkout into a clean directory (git clone --no-hardlinks), installed with npm ci (or the Python equivalent), and the Do command was run once. Commands ran sequentially, with the exit code and wall-clock duration recorded. Durations include only the command, not the install, unless stated.

Operating system Linux 6.18.44
Node and npm Node 22.22.0, npm 10.9.4 for 14 stages; Node 24.21.0, npm 11.19.0 (a scratch install, no project changed) for 2.2, 2.5, 3.3, 3.5 and 4.1

3. Path 1. Screenplay, from the inside out

Why this order: start with the smallest implementation, so the vocabulary is clear before a framework hides it, then see the same pattern under different execution models.

Stage Tool and where Read Do Captured result Watch for
1.1 hand-baked-screenplay-pattern (the project itself) hand-baked ADR-0001 npm test, then npm run verify npm test: 18 files, 128 tests passed, 2.5 s. npm run verify: 128 tests passed, then packs the package (320 files, SHA-256 b1ab47ee…a31) and runs ESM and CommonJS smoke tests; 12.3 s. Treating a teaching provider as a framework.
1.2 Serenity/JS and Playwright in magento-checkout-automation magento ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0004 npm run test:unit 20 tests, 11 suites, 20 passed, 1.8 s. Floating the Serenity/JS version: per-scenario isolation depends on observed v3 behaviour (ADR-0002).
1.3 Cypress and ws in bfx-ws-screenplay bfx ADR-001, ADR-002 npm run test:unit Deviation: npm ci failed because the Cypress binary download arrived truncated (247,831,872 bytes against 248,346,759 expected). With CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0 npm ci it installed in 6.7 s. Then 124 tests, 35 suites, 124 passed, 0.9 s. Converting Cypress command chains into Promises; the core is a port because they conflict (ADR-002). The unit tests never start Cypress, which is why the skipped binary does not matter here.
1.4 Consuming a provider: calculator-screenplay-bdd calculator ADR-0002; poc ADR-0002 npm run check:screenplay-provider PASS: hand-baked-screenplay-pattern 0.3.0 is locked to the approved immutable release, 0.2 s. A relative sibling file:../ path, which both projects moved away from.
1.5 A C# core: tradeblotter-wpf-screenplay (in progress) tradeblotter ADR-0001; docs/screenplay-core.md dotnet test tests/TradeBlotter.Framework.Tests --configuration Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~DriverTests, then dotnet test tests/TradeBlotter.Screenplay.Tests --configuration Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~ScreenplayTests (the outline named no command; these are the project's own in-memory suites from scripts/verify-ci.ps1) Passed (7 October 2026, Windows, .NET 9.0.20, tradeblotter 656620d). DriverTests: exit 0 in 75 s wall clock including restore and build; 29 passed, 0 failed (test run 661 ms). ScreenplayTests: exit 0 in 24 s; 34 passed, 0 failed (565 ms). Both counts equal the counts the project's CI gate asserts (29 and 34). Neither suite opens a desktop window. Letting vendor types leak out of the driver interface.

4. Path 2. One behaviour, many ecosystems

Why this order: contract first, then each runtime, then the gate that checks agreement.

Stage Tool and where Read Do Captured result Watch for
2.1 Gherkin as data: auth-separation scripts/validate-gherkin.mjs npm run lint:gherkin valid Gherkin: 21 scenario(s) across 7 file(s), 0.2 s. Expecting the parser to trace requirements; it validates and counts.
2.2 Cucumber.js: sudoku demoapp001 (Node 24) sudoku README npm test in demoapp001-typescript-cypress 55 scenarios (55 passed), 309 steps (309 passed), 18.7 s. The package declares node >=24 <25, so this stage ran on the scratch Node 24. Comparing counts across runners: this stage counts scenarios and steps, stage 2.3 counts pytest tests. I did not establish that the two numbers cover the same scenarios, so neither is parity evidence; step-text comparison (2.5) is.
2.3 pytest-bdd: sudoku demoapp002 sudoku README python -m pytest in demoapp002-python-pytest 85 passed, 1 warning, 1.0 s. Setup is pip install -c requirements-test.lock -e ".[test]" inside a virtual environment (19.3 s); the first outline omitted this step. The warning is a DeprecationWarning raised inside the gherkin package. Installing without the constraint file, which loses the pinned versions.
2.4 Reqnroll: sudoku demoapp003 sudoku DR-036 dotnet test --no-restore in demoapp003 Passed, after a restore (6 October 2026, Windows, .NET SDK 10.0.401). The command as written exited 1 in 4 s: NETSDK1005: Assets file '…\tests\component\obj\project.assets.json' doesn't have a target for 'net10.0'. Ensure that restore has run. After dotnet restore (exit 0, 5 s), dotnet test --no-restore exited 0 in 28 s: 28 passed (DemoApp003.ComponentTests, net10.0) and 55 passed (DemoApp003.Specs, net10.0), 0 failed, 0 skipped. --no-restore assumes an earlier restore (finding 10). Renaming stable identifiers during a migration; DR-036 kept the legacy ID.
2.5 The parity gate: loan-origination (Node 24), sudoku loan-origination README npm run check:parity Passed, with two deviations (6 October 2026, Windows, Node 24.18.0, Docker 29.0.1). After npm ci (200 s), pip install gherkin-official==42.0.1 (12 s) and npx playwright install chromium (87 s): test:core 33 scenarios (36 s); test:api 85 (60 s); test:angular 106 (271 s); test:nextjs 106 (294 s). The gate then reported PARITY PASS in 6 s: domain-rules 33/33 on core, api, angular and nextjs; workflows 52/52 on api, angular and nextjs; ui-only 21/21 on angular and nextjs; step text identical in each folder. Sudoku's .batch/check-step-text-parity.ps1 exited 0 in 8 s: 217 step lines match across the TypeScript, Python and C# stacks. Deviation 1: on this machine port 8000 was held by an unrelated Docker container (docker-api-1), so the suites ran with PORT=8001, API_PORT=8001 and LOP_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8001; on port 8000 each suite failed with did not become healthy. Deviation 2: npm run check:parity cannot run natively on Windows (finding 8). The unmodified gate was run in a node:24 Linux container against a scratch copy of the four reports with backslashes in their uri fields changed to forward slashes. Treating the gate as a command to run on its own. It reads the four surfaces' reports and fails if any is missing, so a partial run cannot pass.

5. Path 3. Contracts first

Why this order: lint the specification, then check the things a linter cannot, then the semantics.

Stage Tool and where Read Do Captured result Watch for
3.1 Redocly: auth-separation auth-separation ADR-0003 npm run lint:openapi Three specs validated (85, 38 and 19 ms): Your API descriptions are valid, 25 warnings, 1.3 s. Promoting style warnings to errors, or assuming lint validates traffic.
3.2 @asyncapi/parser: auth-separation auth-separation ADR-0003 npm run lint:asyncapi valid AsyncAPI 3.0.0: 4 channel(s), 5 operation(s), 0 warning(s), 1.3 s. Reaching for the CLI when the library lets you assert counts.
3.3 Response validation: sudoku (openapi-backend, Supertest) and loan-origination (Ajv), Node 24 sudoku openapi.contract.test.ts; loan contract.test.ts sudoku npm run test:openapi; loan npm run test:unit Sudoku: 8 tests, 8 passed, 3.5 s, including OpenAPI rejects an intentionally drifted response. Loan: 23 tests in @lop/domain-core and 4 in the Node service, 27 passed, 3.0 s, including serves every documented operation with contract-valid bodies. Validating the specification but never a response. Both suites include a drifted or contract-valid response check, which a lint step cannot give you.
3.4 GraphQL Inspector: saleor (in progress) saleor ADR-001, ADR-003 npm run check:schema (offline baseline) Baseline of 1,482 types loaded; Running in offline deterministic mode (validating baseline self-consistency); self-consistent and valid; 1.0 s. check:schema:live needs a running Saleor and was not run. Reading the offline pass as 'the live schema has not changed'. It checks that the stored snapshot is valid, not that the live API matches it.
3.5 Decimal money: loan-origination (Node 24) loan DR-008 npm run test:core, then npm run check:oracle test:core: 33 scenarios, 8.6 s. check:oracle: Checked 99 expected values across 40 scenarios; Float trap: (400.30 + 300.00) / 2000.00 x 100 formats as 35.01 in IEEE 754; decimal half-even gives 35.02; 0.2 s. The oracle needs pip install gherkin-official==42.0.1 (stated in the README); without it the first run failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gherkin'. Binary floating point for money, or comparing before rounding. The oracle's own output shows a one-hundredth difference from the wrong choice.

6. Path 4. Pin the world

Why this order: own the target, pin it, pin everything around it, learn where pinning stops, then apply the same discipline to documentation.

Stage Tool and where Read Do Captured result Watch for
4.1 A local target: orangehrm (Node 24) orangehrm ADR-0002 npm run test:target-contract Local-only target contract verified for every Cucumber profile, 1.4 s. npm run test:unit: 26 tests, 26 passed, 4.0 s. The package declares node >=24.15.0 <25. Pointing a state-changing suite at a shared public demo.
4.2 Digest-pinned images: saleor (in progress) saleor ADR-004 npm run sut:up Not run in the authoring environment (no Docker daemon). Read-only alternative: read the image references in the compose file against ADR-004. Pinning a tag rather than a digest.
4.3 The whole pinned SUT: parabank parabank DR-PB-10, DR-PB-11 ./scripts/build-sut.ps1 -ValidateImagePinsOnly Ran; reported drift, as designed (6 October 2026, Windows, PowerShell 7.6.6, registry access). Exit 1 in 15 s. Image pin OK: ParaBankRuntime -> tomcat:10.1.57-jre21-temurin-noble@sha256:0d187897…69d3fa, then IMAGE PIN DRIFT: … 'MavenBuilder' is stale: tag 'maven:3.9.16-eclipse-temurin-17-noble' now resolves to 'sha256:1a352420…ed698584', but …\config\container-image-pins.psd1 records 'sha256:880934ae…126737bf'. Review and refresh the pin deliberately. and IMAGE PIN VALIDATION FAIL: 1 of 2 reviewed pins need a deliberate refresh (MavenBuilder). The pin was not refreshed in this run. Afterwards: it was refreshed by PB-PIN-06 (parabank PR #49, merged as 25c83b8 on 7 October 2026 at 08:19:50Z). The same command on main at 25c83b8 then exited 0 in 11 s: Image pin OK: MavenBuilder -> maven:3.9.16-eclipse-temurin-17-noble@sha256:1a352420…ed698584, Image pin OK: ParaBankRuntime -> …@sha256:0d187897…69d3fa, IMAGE PIN VALIDATION PASS: all required tags resolve to their reviewed digests. A dispatched pin-drift run (37593996309) succeeded in 19 s (finding 11). Treating drift as a build failure rather than a reviewed refresh (DR-PB-11).
4.4 Where pinning stops: juice-shop juice-shop docs/dast-lane-design.md, DAST-M3 npm run scan:repeatability Failed on 6 October 2026; passes after a fix. First run (Windows, Node 24.18.0): exit 1 after 6 s, before any container started: dast: repeatability probe 1/3 could not start: spawnSync npm.cmd EINVAL, because scripts/run-repeatability-probe.mjs spawned npm.cmd without a shell, which current Node refuses on Windows. Three fresh Juice Shop and ZAP scans each reported 7 gating classes, the same set (repeatability-reports/summary.json result: PASS; each scan's ZAP baseline showed 0 new failures). On the PR branch it exited 0 in 425 s. The DAST repeatability probe workflow dispatched on the branch (run 37602040336, Linux) passed in 4 min 23 s, with the BDD exploit confirmations at 4 scenarios and 11 steps. The fix adds 6 unit tests (27 in all); 5 of them fail against the old behaviour (finding 7). Assuming a pin guarantees the same coverage.
4.5 Documentation as a pinned artefact: auth-separation's generated Kanban, and the corrected Magento report auth-separation ADR-0004; PR #273 npm run lint:kanban; node portfolio-pedagogical-reports/tools/check-magento-report-vs-compose.mjs lint:kanban: passed, 1.5 s (it fetches portfolio-kanban-generator@1.0.0 through npx, so it needs the network). Comparison, first run (cloud container): a substring test found each of the six version numbers, but 3 for OpenSearch is a weak match, and only two of the six full image strings appear verbatim. Against magento dfa7086: PASS, exit 0, six of six images named and anchored (image lines 27, 60, 79, 99, 108, 127). Against a copy with OpenSearch 3.0 changed to 2.0 and its anchor shifted, it failed with exit 1 on both counts, which the substring test would not have caught. Letting a document restate facts a file already owns.

7. Path 5. What a green result proves

Why last: it reuses tools from the earlier paths and asks of each what it leaves unproven.

Stage Tool and where Read Do Captured result Watch for
5.1 Stryker: hand-baked hand-baked backlog HBSP-34 npm run coverage, then npm run mutate Coverage: 95.99% statements (431/449), 88.57% branches, 97.5% functions, 3.4 s. Mutation: 69.12% score (620 killed, 0 timeouts, 239 survived, 38 no coverage, 0 errors), 116.5 s. Reading coverage as protection. The project's own baseline (3 September 2026) is 69.57% with 4 timeouts; this run's 0 timeouts and 239 survivors give 69.12%. The project documents this: the same 620 mutants are killed either way and timeout classification depends on the machine (docs/mutation-testing.md). Read small movements as noise.
5.2 ZAP passive baseline: juice-shop juice-shop docs/dast-lane-design.md D2.2a; README npm run bdd:dry 4 scenarios (4 skipped), 11 steps (11 skipped), 1.0 s. A dry run reads step definitions; it runs no scan. Expecting a passive scan to find injection, or a dry run to prove a scan.
5.3 axe-core: markdown-renderer markdown-renderer README npm run test:e2e Passed as written (6 October 2026, Windows, Playwright 1.61.1 with its matching Chromium). npm run test:e2e exited 0 in 32 s wall clock: 16 passed (26.3 s reported by Playwright). The earlier cloud-container deviation was a browser-build mismatch, not a fault in the command (finding 3). Reading a pass as WCAG conformance; it checks four states against four rule tags. Also: a green run on a browser other than the pinned one is not the project's own result.

'All passed' covers three emulated projects (desktop Chromium, Pixel on Chromium, iPhone on WebKit), not real devices.
5.5 Native versus mock: tradeblotter (in progress) tradeblotter ADR-0001; docs/benchmark-harness.md ./scripts/run-benchmarks.ps1 -Drivers flaui,ranorex-mock,ranorex -AllowUnavailable from a PowerShell prompt (the outline named no command; this is the one in docs/benchmark-harness.md). Use pwsh -Command, not pwsh -File (finding 12) Passed (7 October 2026, Windows 10.0.26200, .NET 9.0.20, tradeblotter 656620d, clean tree). Exit 0 in 62 s wall clock; it builds the SUT, launches a fresh SUT window per repetition and drives it. Three rows, labelled by mode: flaui Native, PASS, 3 samples, median startup 3,514.03 ms, median lookup mean 255.44 ms, median SUT working set 137.64 MiB; ranorex-mock Mock, MOCK, 0 samples, every figure N/A (Simulated routing only; no WPF automation or performance measurement.); ranorex Native, UNAVAILABLE, 0 samples, every figure N/A (Native Ranorex adapter, SDK and licensed execution are deferred to TB-08B. 8. What the run found

These are findings about the portfolio, kept here because they change what a reader will experience.

  1. The outline omitted a setup step. Stage 2.3 needs pip install -c requirements-test.lock -e ".[test]"; stage 3.5 needs pip install gherkin-official==42.0.1. Both are in the projects' READMEs. Corrected above.
  2. The parity gate cannot give a partial pass. Stage 2.5 shows this directly. It is a property to teach, not a defect.
  3. Two exact commands fail on a machine whose Playwright browsers do not match the pinned version (5.3, 5.4). The projects pin Playwright 1.61.1, which wants Chromium build 1228. On a Windows machine whose Playwright browsers matched, both exact commands passed as written on 6 October 2026 (5.3: 16 tests; 5.4: 31 tests, including the WebKit project), with no npx playwright install. The failure is the browser mismatch, not the commands.
  4. A Cypress binary download can arrive truncated through a proxy (1.3). It does not affect the unit tests.
  5. Node 24 is required by three projects (orangehrm, sudoku demoapp001, and loan-origination, which also accepts Node 22.22.3 or later). The authoring environment's 22.22.0 does not satisfy any of them.
  6. The mutation score on the day was 69.12%, not the baseline's 69.57%, and the project already explains why. Its docs/mutation-testing.md records that the first CI run scored 69.12% against the same commit: 620 mutants killed either way, with the 4 that timed out locally surviving on a faster machine. This run matches that CI figure (620 killed, 0 timeouts, 239 survived). The baseline needs no correction. An earlier version of this section said the backlog figure was wrong; that was my misreading.
  7. The repeatability probe could not start on Windows, and has been fixed (4.4). scripts/run-repeatability-probe.mjs called spawnSync('npm.cmd', …) without a shell, and Node 24.18.0 failed with EINVAL in 6 s. The Linux CI job could never show it. The fix (juice-shop DAST-M5, PR #12, ba76110) starts npm through process.execPath and npm_execpath, with a shell fallback on Windows and plain npm elsewhere. npm_execpath exists only under an npm-launched process, so the fallback is needed for a direct node run. A real-spawn unit test catches the original defect: against the old behaviour it fails with the same EINVAL. The probe then passed on Windows (496 s) and on Linux CI (4 min 23 s). A sweep of every child_process call in the portfolio found one more Windows-only break of the same kind, loan-origination tools/build-reports.mjs (spawnSync('npx') without a shell), recorded in that project's backlog Risk #3.
  8. The parity gate does not run on Windows (2.5). tools/check-parity.mjs fails twice. Line 9 builds the repository root from new URL('..', import.meta.url).pathname, which gives /D:/… and then D:\D:\… (ENOENT … scandir). Past that, Cucumber on Windows records feature URIs with backslashes (..\..\features-shared\domain-rules\…), and line 55 splits them on features-shared/, so it throws Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'split'). The reports and the verdict are sound once the separators are normalised; the gate script is what needs a fix. CI runs on Linux, which is why it passes there.
  9. Port 8000 is not free on a machine running other Docker work. The Node service in test:api, test:angular and test:nextjs defaults to port 8000. Another container held it here and answered /health with 404, so each suite stopped with did not become healthy. PORT (api) and API_PORT (UI suites) override it.
  10. dotnet test --no-restore assumes a restore that a fresh checkout does not have (2.4). On a machine that had not restored the solution at the SDK in use, it exited 1 with NETSDK1005 … doesn't have a target for 'net10.0'. Run dotnet restore first; the tests then pass (83 in all).
  11. The ParaBank build pin was stale on 6 October and has since been refreshed (4.3). MavenBuilder (maven:3.9.16-eclipse-temurin-17-noble) resolved to a different digest from the one recorded in config/container-image-pins.psd1, while ParaBankRuntime still matched. This is the validator doing its job: DR-PB-11 treats it as a reviewed refresh, not a build failure, and the 4.3 run changed nothing. The refresh followed the policy as PB-PIN-06 (plan, six-platform provenance review, full five-command contract, owner merge): parabank PR #49, merge 25c83b8, digest sha256:880934ae…126737bf to sha256:1a352420…ed698584, version and source revision unchanged. Temurin base contents and CVEs were not reviewed. The upstream index can move again, and the weekly pin-drift lane will say so.
  12. pwsh -File does not split a comma list into an array (5.5). pwsh -NoProfile -File ./scripts/run-benchmarks.ps1 -Drivers flaui,ranorex-mock,ranorex failed in 3 s: Cannot validate argument on parameter 'Drivers'. The argument "flaui,ranorex-mock,ranorex" does not belong to the set …. Run it from a PowerShell prompt, or with pwsh -Command "./scripts/run-benchmarks.ps1 -Drivers flaui,ranorex-mock,ranorex -AllowUnavailable", as docs/benchmark-harness.md shows. The script is not at fault.

9. What is not covered

  • Stage 4.2 was not run. It can be run on a Docker machine when the Saleor stack is free; a later edition should replace its label with captured results.
  • Atlas entries with no stage: GitHub Pages, Mermaid and marked, portfolio-prompts, and Claude Code with agent instructions. They describe how the portfolio documents and runs itself, not how it tests, and a possible sixth path was deferred by the owner.
  • The scratch Playwright configuration and the Node 24 install were temporary and are not in any repository.

Provenance: the shape of these paths is recorded in PORTFOLIO_LEARNING_PATHS_OUTLINE_2026-10-06.md, and the run in docs/walkthroughs/2026-10-06_learning-paths-validation.md.
